events.title: Intel 4004 microprocessor introduced
events.summary: Intel introduced the 4004 on November 15, 1971 — the first commercially available microprocessor, a 4-bit CPU with about 2,300 transistors.
events.about: Designed for Busicom calculators, the 4004 proved a full CPU could live on one chip — enabling embedded controllers, hobby computers, and the personal computer revolution. Intel followed with the 8-bit 8008 and 8080 that powered the Altair and early PCs.

narrative.whyChosen: The 4004 was the first microprocessor sold as a commercial product.
narrative.whyImportant: Putting a CPU on a chip made computers cheap enough to embed everywhere.
narrative.problemSolved: Logic boards needed many discrete chips; a single programmable processor cut cost and size.
